correctness.rationale: For fixed point and two-dimensional kernel there are six independent tensor-coordinate conditions, giving projective fiber dimension 29 and incidence dimension 34. Two distinct points can be moved to two independent source slices, so their twelve conditions are independent and the ordered double-incidence has dimension at most 33. At a fixed point, nonuniqueness of the two-dimensional kernel requires rank zero, which imposes nine conditions and gives ambiguity dimension at most 31. Thus a general incidence point has a unique rank-one point and kernel. Combining this with the cited irreducible-image and generic-finiteness input gives a degree-one map in characteristic zero; the projective bundle over a rational base is rational. The packaged coordinate checker and a fresh independent count reproduce 29, 34, 23, 33 and 31.

originality.rationale: The exact primary body could not be independently read in this run, so the comparison to Proposition 4.12 is retained as an access risk. The assigned package, however, isolates a concrete step beyond the cited generic-finiteness input: it proves that tensors with two distinct rank-one points form at most a 33-dimensional locus inside the 34-dimensional incidence and that rank-zero kernel ambiguity has dimension at most 31. In characteristic zero these bounds force the generic finite map to have degree one, giving a rational birational model. Resultary returned only the assigned theorem for this exact rationality claim.

final_claim: The degree-24 divisor of projective 4-by-3-by-3 tensors whose associated matrix space contains a rank-at-most-one matrix is rational: its natural projective-bundle incidence is birational because a general tensor on the divisor has a unique rank-one point and kernel.
limitations: The incidence is only proved birational, not globally one-to-one or an isomorphism.
No rationality claim is made for the GIT quotient itself.
